target_customer: Global consumer brands and content companies that need to find and remove counterfeits, impersonators, gray market sellers and pirated content online
problem: Counterfeits and piracy spread across thousands of marketplaces and sites, and brands lack scalable tools and legal expertise to detect and enforce.
business_model: B2B AI managed service and SaaS for brand protection with attached legal enforcement (MarqLaw); self serve pricing from 99 dollars a month listed on the site
product_category: AI brand protection and IP enforcement software

founders.name: Mark Lee
founders.background_notes: From the YC page. The company description says it was founded by Harvard Law graduates, but only Mark Lee is listed; other founders were not found. Company bio says he splits time between Seoul and Los Angeles.

competitors.name: BrandShield
competitors.what: Online brand protection and counterfeit takedown service

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision detection across 1,500 platforms plus takedown workflows is standard machine learning engineering at scale; the harder part is enforcement operations and legal process.

defensibility.rationale: Enforcement history, platform relationships and brand integrations compound, but several established brand protection vendors compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was found through 2026; the company raised a 48 million dollar Series B in 2025 and remains private.

market_need_then: The Block coverage of the 2022 round links the product to NFT and consumer counterfeit detection, and the company claims LVMH's 2022 Innovation Award; dated 2021 market size figures were not found.

identity.logo: a refreshed brand identity was unveiled alongside the Series B in September 2025; details not described
identity.voice_and_tone: mission driven about protecting original ideas and creativity

rebrands.why: Unveiled with the Series B announcement; reason not stated

brand_strength.rationale: Strong B2B recognition via LVMH accelerator and funding coverage, but the name MarqVision is confusable with the unrelated Marq (formerly Lucidpress) brand in search results.

outcome_analysis: MarqVision, founded in 2020, joined YC in Summer 2021 and grew into a roughly 200 to 260 person company serving about 350 brand partners, raising a Series A in 2022, an extension in 2024 and a 48 million dollar Series B in September 2025 from Peak XV, Salesforce Ventures and others. Its enterprise sales motion and legal services layer drive growth, and the company remains private with no distress found.
notes: A 5M seed in Sept 2021 appears only on one aggregator and is not recorded. 2022 Series A is 20M per The Block and 25M per Startupintros; the lower figure is used. The 2024 extension is 22 billion won (about 16.5M) per KED Global, with Seedtable naming a different lead (Atinum vs Altos). Series B lead: Peak XV per company and most outlets, ZoomInfo says Salesforce Ventures. Company states about 90M total raised; aggregators range 84M to 94M. Competitor list lacks a dated pre-batch source; Red Points, Corsearch and OpSec did not surface in search.
